paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Before Jesus preaches one sermon or heals one person, His Father speaks over Him: "You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased." (Luke 3:22) Jesus hasn't done His ministry yet. The Father is pleased with Him first, and that's a love nobody has to earn.

Now look at WHO gets baptized. Jesus steps into the water right along with everybody else (Luke 3:21). He doesn't stand off to the side. I think that's how He shows He's here for the crowd, and that means He's here for you, baker.

And then that family line. Luke says Jesus "was regarded as the son of Joseph" and runs the line back through David and Abraham, all the way to Adam, "the son of God." (Luke 3:23, 31, 34, 38) Those are real names and real people, and the One the Father calls His beloved Son came into that family. So take this with you: the Father loves His Son, the Son came to be with us, and that's good news you can stand on.
